title: The Bear and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Bear was once bragging about his generous feelings, and saying how refined he was compared with other animals. (There is, in fact, a tradition that a Bear will never touch a dead body.) A Fox, who heard him talking in this strain, smiled and said, "My friend, when you are hungry, I only wish you _would_ confine your attention to the dead and leave the living alone." A hypocrite deceives no one but himself.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Bear bragging about?
options: His strength compared to the Fox

questions.prompt: According to the tradition mentioned in the passage, what will a Bear never do?
According to the passage, who overheard the Bear's boasting?
According to the passage, what does the Fox say he wishes the Bear would do?
options: Share his food with the Fox
Confine his attention to the dead and leave the living alone
Teach the Fox how to hunt

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "refined" mean in "how refined he was"?
As the passage uses it, what does "strain" mean in "talking in this strain"?
options: A manner or style of speaking

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Fox's remark a pointed criticism of the Bear's boast?
options: It proves the Bear has never actually met a dead body
It shows the Fox is jealous of the Bear's reputation
It suggests the Bear's claim to refinement means little since he still preys on living creatures
It reveals the Fox wants to become a bear

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Bears are more dangerous than foxes
Claiming a virtue does not make it true if one's actions say otherwise
Foxes should avoid talking to bears

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Bear compare himself to other animals?
options: He said he was larger than other animals
He said he was faster than other animals
He said he was more refined than other animals
He said he was older than other animals

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox do just before speaking to the Bear?
According to the passage, how does the Fox address the Bear when he speaks?
As the passage uses it, what does "confine" mean in "confine your attention to the dead"?
Based on the passage, what does the closing line "A hypocrite deceives no one but himself" suggest about the Bear?
options: The Bear has successfully convinced every other animal of his refinement
The Bear is unaware that a Fox is listening to him
The Bear plans to stop hunting living animals
The Bear's claims of refinement do not change his true nature, whatever he tells himself

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox and a Bear compete to see who is more refined
A Bear proves his refinement by refusing to eat a dead body in front of the Fox
A Bear boasts of his refinement, but a Fox points out that he still preys on the living, exposing the boast as hollow
A Fox teaches a Bear how to hunt more humanely
